observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: The receiver is ECX, used directly by 0x00c47cc7 CMP dword ptr [ECX + 0x84],EAX. observed_mechanics: 0x00c47cc0: MOV EAX,[ESP + 0x4] hoists the argument before the frame exists, which is what identifies it as a caller stack argument rather than a local.
0x00c47cc7 CMP dword ptr [ECX + 0x84],EAX with 0x00c47ccd JZ 0x00c47d6c is the idempotence guard: setting the value the receiver already holds does nothing at all, not even the buffer resets.
0x00c47cd3: MOV dword ptr [ECX + 0x84],EAX is the only unconditional receiver write, and it happens before the buffer resets.

0x00c47cd9..0x00c47cf2 and 0x00c47cf8..0x00c47d11 are two structurally identical arms: compare head against tail, and if they differ write a 16-bit zero through the head and copy the head into the tail. The head is re-read from the receiver after the store rather than reused from the register, which is why the tail is set to the head's value and not to the compared value.
0x00c47ce9 and 0x00c47d08 use MOV word ptr [EAX],DX after XOR EDX,EDX, so exactly two bytes are cleared and the following wchar_t is untouched: a one-element string truncation, not a memset.
0x00c47d17 CMP dword ptr [ECX + 0x84],0x3 reads the field back rather than reusing the argument register, so the special path triggers on the STORED value.
0x00c47d20 stores the immediate 0x038cf2fd at frame offset +0x30 and 0x00c47d3e stores 0 at +0x38; these are the only non-pointer immediates in the body.
0x00c47d28 writes 0x013eb90c to frame offset +0 and 0x00c47d37 overwrites the same dword with 0x013eb844, so the first store is dead.
0x00c47d35 XCHG dword ptr [EAX],EDX with EDX zeroed by 0x00c47d2f stores a zero to frame offset +0x04.
0x00c47d46 stores the receiver to frame offset +0x08, so the temporary carries a back-pointer to the caller.
0x00c47d4a CALL 0x0067dcc0 is the SDK-named App::IAppSystem::Get, whose whole body is MOV EAX,[0x015fd890] ; RET.
0x00c47d4f and 0x00c47d51 load the app system's vtable and its slot +0x14; 0x00c47d60/0x00c47d62 dispatch it thiscall with ECX = the app system.
0x00c47d54/0x00c47d5a/0x00c47d5f push three stack arguments in the order 0, &frame+0, 0x038cf2fd; because arguments are pushed right to left the callee signature is (0x038cf2fd, &temporary, 0).
0x00c47d64 LEA ECX,[ESP] followed by 0x00c47d67 CALL 0x00421cf0 runs the temporary's destructor on the same object the slot +0x14 call received.
0x00c47d6f: RET 0x4 is the proof that the callee, not the caller, pops the single argument.

sdk_correspondence.observation: The Ghidra decompiler types the stack temporary as CommandLine and calls the 0x0067dcc0 result IAppSystem. The IAppSystem half is defensible because 0x0067dcc0 carries the SDK-imported name and its body is a single global load. The CommandLine half is REJECTED. Spore ModAPI's Spore/App/CommandLine.h declares ASSERT_SIZE(CommandLine, 0x38) with mSplits at +0x04, field_18 at +0x18 and field_28 at +0x28. The temporary built here is walked by 0x00421cf0 as 32 eight-byte pairs from byte offset +0x08, reaching byte offset +0x108, and its selector mask aliases pair[6].first at +0x38. A 0x38-byte object cannot satisfy that walk, so the temporary is not an App::CommandLine and the decompiler's type is a guess.
sdk_correspondence.not_asserted: Neither the name CommandLine nor any App::CommandLine ownership is claimed for this target.

semantic_contract: Assign a new state value to the receiver. If the receiver already holds that value the call is a complete no-op: no field is written, neither wide buffer is touched, and the app system is not consulted. Otherwise the state word at receiver+0x84 is overwritten, and then each of two wide buffers whose head and tail cursors differ is truncated by one element - a 16-bit zero is written through the head cursor and the tail cursor is moved back to the head. When, and only when, the newly stored value is exactly 3, a stack temporary of at least 0x3c bytes is built: vtable 0x013eb844 at offset +0x00, a zero at +0x04, the receiver at +0x08, the immediate 0x038cf2fd at +0x30 and a zero selector mask at +0x38. The app system is then fetched from the global 0x015fd890 and its vtable slot +0x14 is called with (0x038cf2fd, &temporary, 0), after which the temporary is destroyed by 0x00421cf0, which - because the mask is zero - only rewrites the temporary's vtable pointer. The receiver is never null-checked.
classification_rationale: Not STRONG_SEMANTIC: the whole body, the callee-cleaned ABI, every field offset, every constant, the buffer-reset shape and the dispatch slot are read from live disassembly and corroborated by 18 callsites including a 7-way jump table, but the owning class, the temporary's class, the meaning of the state value and the callee behind slot +0x14 are all unestablished, which is a material element. Not STRUCTURAL_ONLY: the idempotence rule, the two reset arms and the value-3 tail are genuine behavioural claims and the whole function is reconstructed. The bound is named: owning type, state-value semantics, and the slot +0x14 callee.
semantic_findings: The function is the single point of assignment for the state word at receiver+0x84, and it is idempotent, so a redundant set is free of side effects including the app-system call.
Exactly one state value, 3, has an externally visible side effect. The other attested values 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 only reset the two buffers.

The two buffer reset arms are identical in shape, so the two buffers are almost certainly the same container type; the head/tail cursor pair is the only layout evidence and no length or capacity field was observed.
The truncation writes exactly two bytes, so it clears one wchar_t at the head and leaves the rest of the buffer alone.

The state-3 temporary is a request/queue object rather than a CommandLine: the destructor walks 32 optional sub-objects selected by a bitmask, and the vtable at 0x013eb844 is immediately followed by the format string 'queuing %ls for bake' at 0x013eb850.
Because the selector mask is written as zero, the state-3 path performs no per-slot teardown; the 32-pair walk is dead on this path and exists for other constructors of the same object.
0x00421cf0 stores three different vtable addresses in sequence, 0x013eb844 then 0x013eb90c then 0x013eb918, and the last one wins, which is the classic inlined chain of base-class destructors.

The immediate 0x038cf2fd is below the image base 0x00400000, so it is a key or identifier and not a pointer. The same neighbourhood carries a family of similar literals (0x7bac9736, 0x131a9f54, 0x02aa5ada, 0x0578f7f8, 0x0105a93d, 0xeeee8218), which is consistent with a hashed lookup key space.
unresolved_questions: What class owns this function? 18 live references, all UNCONDITIONAL_CALL, and no DATA reference, so it is not a vtable slot and no owner can be named.
What do the state values mean? Values 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and one dynamically forwarded value are attested; 0, 4 and negatives are not excluded. No enum name is claimed.

What class is the stack temporary? Its vtable 0x013eb844 has three dwords and is followed by the 'queuing %ls for bake' format string, and its destructor walks 32 masked pairs, but no class name is asserted.
What is 0x038cf2fd? It is below the image base so it cannot be a pointer, and it is passed as the callee's first argument. It is a key or id of unknown derivation.
What is the concrete callee at app-system vtable slot +0x14? 0x015fd890 is zero in the file image, so no table address was ever observable.
What are the two wide buffers at receiver+0x14c/+0x150 and +0x15c/+0x160, and what populates them? Only the reset shape is observed; no producer of their contents was located in this batch.
Why does the state-3 path pass 0 as the third argument and a non-null pointer as the second? The callee signature beyond those three dwords is unknown.
Is the dead store at 0x00c47d28 (0x013eb90c) meaningful to any runtime patching or vtable interposition scheme, or is it plain compiler residue?
No original-process trace exists, so the state-value distribution and the buffer contents are unverified.

runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists for this address. In particular 0x015fd890 was never observed populated, so the app-system slot +0x14 callee is unknown at runtime as well as statically.
The Cell stage has never been entered in any recorded run, so the real distribution of state values and the real contents of the two wide buffers are unverified.
A differential fixture would need a real receiver plus a populated app-system singleton, neither of which static evidence supplies.

body_reconstruction.claim_scope: The 178-byte body is reconstructed in full, including the idempotence guard, both buffer-reset arms, the value-3 gate, the five temporary stores in their original order and the argument order of the slot +0x14 call. No class name, no enum name and no CommandLine identity is claimed; the two external ports are declared, not implemented.
